newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA PREPARES TO APPOINT AGRICULTURE COUNCIL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA PREPARES TO APPOINT AGRICULTURE COUNCIL.

text.p: South African legislators will interview 30 nominees for a new 10-member Agricultural Marketing Council in Cape Town on December 17 and 18.
Parliamentary agriculture committee chairperson Janet Love ruled after a meeting on Friday that details of the candidates would not be released immediately.
She said their curricula vitae would be released when interviewing starts, but said she would ask the nominees for permission to release the information next week.
"Obviously, the committee will take account of that if anyone decides not to release their c.v. ahead of the interviews," she said after the meeting.
The parliamentary committee has a month from today to trim the shortlist of 30 nominees to 15.
The names will then be forwarded to Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom, who will appoint 10 of the finalists to the council, which will assume the oversight role of the existing marketing boards.
In terms of the Agricultural Marketing Act approved by parliament this year, the council should comprise two members each from five designated sectors.

The sectors are commercial agriculture, agricultural product-related trade and industry, agricultural economics including international marketing, agriculture-related consumer issues and production and marketing by small-scale and previously disadvantaged farmers.
Love said up to five of the council members could be appointed as full or part-time salaried members. The rest would serve on a voluntary basis.

The council will be empowered to consider requests by agricultural sectors for limited control measures, including price control, but is obliged to oversee the phasing out of existing marketing boards.
Interventions approved by the council will be for limited periods and to address specific short-term problems.
